introduction.arc: This itinerary threads WWII history across Britain and Normandy before closing in Porto. London nights are at 53 Greek Street in Soho. Wednesday Oct 14 is Imperial War Museum, Borough Market, dinner at Funky Noodle, then Operation Mincemeat at the Fortune Theatre. Thursday Oct 15 is Churchill War Rooms and the Kensington Royal Village walk; dinner that night is TBD. Other London days are still high-level ideas only (Battle of Britain Bunker, Bletchley Park, Tank Museum Bovington maybe overnight). Sunday Oct 18 flies Heathrow to Paris Orly (BA8137); the Orly hotel that night is TBD. Three nights in Bayeux cover the American Sector tour with Objective Normandy, a self-guided Bayeux day, and Mont-Saint-Michel — how you get from Orly to Bayeux on Oct 19 is not specified. Thursday Oct 22 flies Orly to Porto (TP455) to the Ribeira apartment. The return TAP TP211 OPO→EWR (7:30 PM–11:55 PM) has no date in Jon’s email; this guide assumes Oct 26 from the Porto checkout — confirm with Jon.
introduction.differentiators: Three Airbnbs are on the books plus one missing Orly hotel: London HMFRRRZRTN at 53 Greek St; Bayeux HMKWYPDKBE at 4 Rue Franche; Porto HM549AK8C2 at Rua dos Mercadores 77, 3rd floor. London to Normandy is LHR→ORY (BA8137), an Orly hotel TBD, then an unspecified transfer to Bayeux. The Bayeux Tapestry Museum remains closed for renovation through October 2027; the tapestry itself is on loan at the British Museum in London (10 Sep 2026 – Jul 2027) during these London days.

items.text: Leisurely morning, hotel breakfast

items.why: Consecrated 1077, the original home of the Bayeux Tapestry for nearly 700 years before it moved to a dedicated museum.

items.text: Lunch in the town center

Musée Mémorial de la Bataille de Normandie (Battle of Normandy Memorial Museum) — self-guided
items.why: NOTE: the Bayeux Tapestry Museum is closed for renovation (Sept 2025–Oct 2027) and will not be open during this trip — this museum, covering the Battle of Normandy itself, is the substitute for a Bayeux museum day. Real uniforms, vehicles, and a diorama of the full campaign.

items.text: Bayeux War Cemetery — the largest British and Commonwealth WWII cemetery in France — 4,144 Commonwealth graves plus roughly 500 more of other nationalities (mostly German), 4,648 burials in total, directly across the road from the museum
Walk back into central Bayeux to Le Volet Qui Penche — approx. 12 min from the cemetery/museum area

items.text: Livraria Lello — the bookshop long rumored to have inspired Hogwarts library
items.why: The neo-Gothic staircase and stained-glass ceiling make Lello one of the world's most beautiful bookshops. J.K. Rowling did live in Porto in the early '90s while writing early Harry Potter material, but the specific claim that Lello inspired Hogwarts's library is a popular, widely-repeated legend she has publicly and explicitly denied (2020: "I was never inspired by Lello's, I didn't even enter it") — worth knowing before repeating it as fact on-site.

contact.booking_note: Buy timed-entry ticket online 1–2 days ahead to skip the queue.
